The home-screen icon: pick one of nine

Each icon is the 180 px file an iPhone asks for. iOS 26 lays its glass over every icon saved from a web page, and that glass is what made A look rough. The glass here is drawn by this page, so it is a close guess and not the phone itself. Say the letter you like. The next PR makes the real icons from it.

The drawn glass: a white lift over the whole tile, every edge softened a little, a band along the bottom that blurs and lifts more, and a bright rim. The phone does more than this. A photo of the real home screen decides.

Ten-second check on any iOS 26 phone: Settings, Accessibility, Display & Text Size, Reduce Transparency. If the icon snaps crisp, it is the glass. Turn it back off after.

A is the icon live since v2.4227. The favicon and the CountTooling and Takeoff Tooling marks do not change with this pick.
